web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Ten Years Under the Microscope: Earnings Quality, Debt & Litigation Liabilities
question: Over a full 10-year cycle, how clean is McKesson's cash conversion, why is book equity negative, and how much real leverage sits behind the balance sheet?

epigraph.quote: Net income is an opinion; ten years of operating cash flow minus capex—after paying real litigation settlements—is a fact.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: From FY2017 to FY2026 (fiscal years ended March 31), McKesson more than doubled revenue from $198.53 billion to $403.43 billion. That marks an 8.2% compound annual growth rate [15]. GAAP operating income recovered from the FY2021 opioid trough (-$5.04 billion) to a record $6.21 billion in FY2026 (+40% YoY) [2, 15]. GAAP net income hit $5.10 billion ($4.76 billion attributable to McKesson) [2, 15]. Operating cash flow stayed steady across all ten years. It never fell below $4.04 billion even during the pandemic and opioid years, reaching $6.16 billion in FY2026 [2, 15].

web_blocks.caption: McKesson 10-Year Audited Financial Forensics (FY2017–FY2026, USD Billions)
web_blocks.takeaway: *Note: FY2026 PP&E capex was $0.44B ($436M); including $309M capitalized software, total capex was $745M and company-defined FCF was $5.41B [2]. Across 10 years, cumulative CFO exceeded $48B with zero negative cash-flow years.

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: Negative Book Equity, Debt & Litigation Claims

web_blocks.html: A quick screen of McKesson's balance sheet flashes a startling number: stockholders' deficit of -$2,172 million at March 31, 2026. That widened to -$3,950 million at September 30, 2026 [2, 15]. In McKesson's case, negative book equity is not distress. It reflects $32,005 million in cumulative share buybacks sitting as a deduction against $22,291 million in retained earnings [2].

Forensic discipline still requires counting all debt-like claims. On March 31, 2026, McKesson held $3,975 million in cash and $6,526 million in total debt ($1,267M short-term and $5,259M long-term) [2]. Net financial debt was a modest $2,551 million, or ~0.36x FY2026 EBITDA of $7.18B [2, 15]. By September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY2027), cash rose to $6.53 billion ahead of the November 2026 PMG close, with ~$11.5 billion in total liquidity [8, 9, 15]. Beyond bank debt, analysts must count two senior claims. First, long-term opioid liabilities stand at $5,091 million ($5,058M on June 30, 2026) [2, 21]. They took $684 million in cash in FY2026 and run through 2038 [2, 21]. Second, redeemable noncontrolling interests stand at $2,563 million (up from $943M on March 31, 2026 after Apollo's Med-Surg stake) [3].

web_blocks.caption: Forensic Capital Structure & Senior Claims Summary (March 31, 2026 vs. Q1/Q2 FY2027)
rows: Pre-funded ahead of $2.25B PMG cash close on Nov 2, 2026 [5]
Opioid settlement run-off through 2038 (-$684M cash in FY26) [2]
Put-like physician MSO & Apollo Med-Surg claims [3, 9]

web_blocks.takeaway: McKesson's core financial leverage is conservative (<1x net debt/EBITDA), but an honest enterprise-value accounting must treat the $5.06B opioid liability and $2.56B redeemable noncontrolling interests as debt-like claims.

web_blocks.title: Accounting Quality Check: LIFO, Goodwill & Non-GAAP Adjustments
paragraphs: McKesson uses Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) accounting for U.S. drug inventories. That creates non-cash swings (a $210M LIFO credit in FY2026 vs. an $82M charge in FY2025) that management strips out of Adjusted Earnings [2].

Goodwill ($11,316M) and net intangibles ($4,079M) jumped in FY2026 from Core Ventures and PRISM Vision, and will rise again with PMG ($2.25B) [2, 8]. Tracking organic cash conversion and post-deal ROIC remains vital.

web_blocks.html: Overall, McKesson's ten-year cash conversion is elite. Cumulative operating cash flow topped $48 billion from FY2017 to FY2026 with zero down years [15]. Treating the $5.06 billion opioid liability and $2.56 billion redeemable minority interests as debt-like claims keeps our valuation honest [2, 3, 21]. Meanwhile, rising goodwill ($11,316M) from Core Ventures, PRISM Vision, and PMG ($2.25B) makes post-deal ROIC a key item to track [2, 8].

book_paragraphs: When a company boasts of steady earnings growth, my first step is to pull ten years of cash flow statements. I want to see if the cash actually showed up in the bank. In McKesson's case, the ten-year audit tells a clear story—with two caveats you must adjust for. Cash flow is always harder to fake than accounting profit.

Look at the decade from fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2026 [15]. Revenue more than doubled from $198.5 billion to $403.4 billion [15]. Along the way, GAAP operating income swung wildly: $7.1 billion in 2017, $762 million in 2018, negative $5.04 billion in 2021 on the opioid charge, and $6.21 billion in 2026 [2, 15]. Now look at operating cash flow across those same ten years: $4.74B, $4.34B, $4.04B, $4.37B, $4.54B, $4.43B, $5.16B, $4.31B, $6.08B, $6.16B [15]. Not a single down-cycle year. Every year, $4 billion to $6 billion of real cash poured in—even after $684 million in opioid cash payouts in fiscal 2026 [2]. Across the full decade, cumulative operating cash flow exceeded $48 billion [15].

Now address the weirdest line on McKesson's balance sheet. Stockholders' equity is negative $2.17 billion at March 31, 2026, and negative $3.95 billion by September 30, 2026 [2, 15]. Does that mean McKesson is broke? Not at all. Look one line higher: McKesson has earned $22.3 billion in retained earnings, but it bought back $32.0 billion of its own stock [2]. Because GAAP deducts treasury stock from book equity, big buyback compounders often show negative book value—just like Home Depot or McDonald's. That accounting rule reflects cash returned to owners, not balance-sheet weakness.

Still, a careful analyst never stops at bank debt. Yes, net financial debt of $2.55 billion at fiscal year-end is small next to $7.18 billion of EBITDA [2, 15]. Yet two other senior claims stand ahead of common shareholders. First is the $5.06 billion opioid liability, which takes several hundred million dollars of cash each year through 2038 [2, 21]. Second is $2.56 billion in redeemable noncontrolling interests—doctor put options in Core Ventures and PRISM Vision, plus Apollo's preferred stake in Wellverse [3, 9]. When we value the business in Chapter 7, we will add those real claims to debt so our math stays honest. That way, we never understate the true enterprise value of the business.

One more accounting detail deserves a quick check: LIFO inventory accounting and goodwill [2]. McKesson uses Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) rules for U.S. drug stock, creating non-cash quarterly swings like a $210 million credit in FY2026 versus an $82 million charge in FY2025 [2]. Management rightly removes those swings from adjusted earnings. Meanwhile, goodwill hit $11.32 billion and net intangibles reached $4.08 billion in FY2026 after Core Ventures and PRISM Vision, and both will rise with the $2.25 billion PMG deal [2, 8]. Watching organic cash conversion confirms those acquisitions earn real returns.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Ten years of $4B–$6B annual operating cash flow on <0.2% capex-to-sales proves McKesson is an elite cash compounder. Treating the $5.06B opioid liability and $2.56B redeemable minority interests as debt-like claims keeps our balance-sheet math honest.
